content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a project where I need to independently control three motors at variable speeds. Since I'm familiar with [product_name], I considered using it to manage the three drives, communicating via Modbus. I understand that one drive can be directly connected to [product_name], but I'm unsure if it's feasible to connect multiple drives or how to achieve this setup. Do I need expansion modules or an Ethernet switch? Appreciate any advice.

This approach won't work because Modbus TCP/IP and Modbus RTU are different protocols. The [product_name] supports only Modbus TCP/IP, while the V20 inverter supports only Modbus RTU or USS. Referring to the V20 manual: it supports communication with PLCs from [company_name] via USS over RS485. You must specify whether RS485 uses USS or MODBUS RTU, with USS as default. For RS485, a shielded twisted pair cable is recommended. A different controller such as [version_no] would be more appropriate. Example: Speed Control of a V20 with [version_no] using protocol conversion.

Hi, Alternatively, you can use a Modbus RTU/Modbus TCP/IP Gateway, such as devices from moxa or ADF. However, in practice, gateways may have limitations and unreliable performance. For a stable and trustworthy solution, it's best to follow the previous advice and select [version_no] for the task. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Discussion centered around difficulties using [product_name] to control multiple drives via Modbus, primarily due to protocol incompatibility—[product_name] supports Modbus TCP/IP, while the drives only offer Modbus RTU or USS. Participants pointed out the practical issues of protocol converters and leaned towards recommending a more compatible controller, noting the importance of clear protocol documentation and user experiences regarding system integration.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks a simple, reliable solution for controlling three drives through [product_name] over Modbus, possibly using expansion modules or network hardware. They expect straightforward connectivity and dependable operation.
